decisions.reason: After four years the market signal should be clearer, but as a resin-processing unit in the firm's core application domain it still has enough strategic fit and serviceability to justify staying on the market unless demand has proven distinctly weak.

This product remains close to the firm's technical base, yet because it overlaps with another two-component resin injection unit the case for portfolio consolidation is somewhat stronger if sales have not differentiated clearly.

An automatic airless spray gun is a natural extension of the firm's established spray-application range, so keeping it available is relatively low cost and consistent with serving industrial customers with varied automation needs.
A manual airless spray gun sits squarely in the firm's core portfolio and likely benefits from stable replacement and complementary demand, making withdrawal within the next year unlikely.

As a multi-model air-assisted airless spray-gun line in a central product category, it offers broad coverage across customer segments and therefore retains high option value with low reason to exit now.
